Subject: Marketplace billing: how will platform fee show on invoice?

Hi Rishi,

Quick question as we finalize procurement: when a customer buys via CloudPartner's listing (GCP), how will invoices split between Redwood and CloudPartner look from the buyer side? Specifically: 

- Will the platform/service fee appear as a separate line on the invoice we receive from CloudPartner?
- For EU VAT handling, which party is responsible for VAT on the platform fee vs. the usage?
- We can provide a signed W-8BEN-E for our US entity — does that need to go to both Redwood and CloudPartner or just one party?

I'm attaching a mock invoice from our AP team (sample-co-sell-invoice-split.csv) and our W-8BEN-E (FintechCo_W8BEN-E_signed.pdf). We'd like to close PO and get the first month's usage rolling.

Subject: Re: Marketplace billing: how will platform fee show on invoice?

Hi Sara — thanks for the attachments, they help. Short answers up front, then specifics below so AP has a record.

- Invoice appearance: In GCP co-sell setups, the buyer often receives a consolidated invoice from the marketplace/reseller (CloudPartner). That invoice should show: usage lines (our SKU) + a separate line for the platform/reseller fee if CloudPartner chooses to surface it. Redwood does not control the reseller's invoice template.

- VAT responsibility (EU): VAT treatment depends on whether the reseller is acting as a principal or agent and on the EU reverse-charge applicability. If CloudPartner is the supplier on the invoice (principal), they collect VAT according to their VAT registration. If they act as agent, the reverse charge can apply and VAT may be accounted by the buyer.

- W-8BEN-E: For US tax withholding (nonresident vendor) the W-8BEN-E should be provided to whichever US payer is remitting payment to your entity. If CloudPartner is the payor, provide to them. However, Redwood also requests a copy when the contract or settlement flow routes through Redwood (we need it for our records and for some marketplace settlement reconciliation).

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Tom (CloudPartner) — can you confirm whether CloudPartner will show a separate platform/reseller fee line on customer invoices and whether you act as principal or agent for the FintechCo listing?
2) Sara — please confirm which legal entity will appear on the PO and whether FintechCo wants VAT evidence/exemption applied at purchase time.

Attaching a short checklist below for AP signal.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
AP checklist (for buyer):
- Confirm invoice recipient entity and billing address.
- Confirm reseller role (principal vs agent) with partner.
- Provide W-8/W-9 to payor(s) and copy to Redwood for records.
- If EU buyer: request VAT number validation and specify whether reverse charge applies.

From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@cloudpartner.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace billing: how will platform fee show on invoice?

Thanks Rishi / Sara — quick clarification from our side: CloudPartner will be the billing principal for the FintechCo listing on GCP (we bill the customer directly and remit to Redwood as part of our settlement). We currently show a single consolidated invoice to the buyer with separate line items for each SKU and a distinct "Platform Fee" line when applicable (so your AP can see the split).

On VAT: for EU customers we collect VAT based on our registration. We can also mark lines as reverse-charge eligible when the buyer provides a valid EU VAT number; however, our invoice template still shows the gross value and a note about reverse-charge.

W-8BEN-E: please send that to partnerbilling@cloudpartner.com. We'll retain it for our US tax withholding records. Rishi / Redwood — if you want a copy for your settlement reconciliation, ask the customer to CC you when they send it; we don't automatically share their tax docs.

Tom

Thanks Tom — that's helpful. Quick internal note for FintechCo's AP (copying the customer thread so they have the ask): 

1) Because CloudPartner is principal and issues the invoice, FintechCo should:
   - Send the signed W-8BEN-E to partnerbilling@cloudpartner.com (Tom confirmed).
   - CC rishi@redwood.com so Redwood can attach a copy to our settlement record (this avoids delays during payout reconciliation).

2) If FintechCo wants reverse-charge handling on EU VAT lines, please provide your VAT registration number at time of purchase and request the partner mark the invoice accordingly. Note that reverse-charge is an accounting treatment — CloudPartner's template will still show VAT fields but with a reverse-charge note when applicable.

3) For AP automation: we've included the sample-co-sell-invoice-split.csv into our settlement-run playbook. We'll map the Platform Fee as a separate settlement line so your finance team can reconcile credits/remittances from CloudPartner to Redwood.

If there's anything else (e.g., W-9 required for US entities, local withholding for APAC), loop back and we'll scope the evidence required.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
